v: Understand why scams work
Recognise the common tricks

b.v: About 15 minutes. Share each lesson with your parents and children too.

v: Hurry - 'Your account will be blocked in 10 minutes'
Fear - 'Police case against you', 'Your SIM will be closed'
Greed - 'You won a prize', 'Earn Rs 5,000 a day from home'
Fake prize and lucky draw messages asking for a 'processing fee'
Fake messages about government support money asking for codes or fees
Calls pretending to be your bank asking for card details or a code
Fake job offers abroad that ask for money first
A 'friend' on chat who suddenly needs money urgently

b.v: If a message or call makes you hurry, fear or feel lucky, stop. Hang up, wait, and check yourself through an official number or website. Real banks and offices never mind if you call them back.
Do this now:|Look at your messages and find one that uses hurry, fear or greed.|Tell one family member the golden rule today.

day-2.t: Day 2 — Strong passwords and two-step login

v: Make passwords hard to guess
Turn on two-step login on your main accounts
Long: at least 12 characters
A phrase is easy to remember: 'Chai-at-4-with-Ammi!'
Different for every important account
Never your name, phone number, CNIC or date of birth

b.v: Use the password manager built into your phone or browser, or a trusted password manager app. If you write passwords down, keep the notebook at home in a safe place, never in your wallet or phone gallery.

With two-step login, a thief needs your password and also a code from your phone. Turn it on for your email first - whoever controls your email can reset all your other accounts - then for social media, chat apps and XpertCreation.
Do this now:|Change the password of your main email to a long phrase.|Turn on two-step login for your email.

v: Understand what one-time codes are for
Never be tricked into sharing one

b.v: A one-time code (OTP) is like the key to your house for one minute. It lets someone log in to your account, move money or take over your chat on a new phone. Whoever has the code can act as you.

v: No bank, telecom company, courier or government office will ever ask you for a code
Read the message: it often says 'Do not share this code'
If someone asks for a code, it is a scam - every time
'I sent a code to your number by mistake, please send it back'
'Your parcel is waiting, tell me the code to confirm the address'
'This is your bank, tell me the code to stop the fraud'

b.v: If you already shared a code, act now: open the account, log out other devices, change the password and call your bank on its official helpline.
Do this now:|Tell your parents: never share any code with anyone.|Save your bank's official helpline in your contacts.

day-4.t: Day 4 — Keep your chat account safe

v: Stop people taking over your chat account
Know the signs of a hacked friend

b.v: Step by step:|Open the settings of your chat app.|Find Account, then two-step verification.|Set a 6-digit PIN that is not your birthday and add your email.|Do the same on XpertChat and other apps that offer it.
Chat apps can be opened on a computer or another phone. Check 'Linked devices' in settings and log out anything you don't recognise.
3) When a friend asks for money

v: Call them on their normal number and hear their voice
Ask something only they would know
Scammers who take over an account message everyone in the contact list

b.v: Do this now:|Turn on the PIN in your chat app.|Check linked devices and remove unknown ones.

day-5.t: Day 5 — Fake links and fake websites

v: Check a link before tapping it
Spot fake websites
Who sent it? A stranger, or a friend sending something unusual?
Long press the link to see the real address
Short links hide where they go
Spelling tricks: 'xpertcreatlon.com' instead of 'xpertcreation.com'
Look at the address bar, not the logo - anyone can copy a logo
Prices that are far too low are a warning
Only cash-on-delivery or advance payment to a personal account is a warning
No real address or phone, or reviews that all sound the same

b.v: 3) If you entered details on a fake page
Step by step:|Change that password at once, on the real website.|If it was a card or bank login, call your bank's helpline to block it.|Turn on two-step login.
Do this now:|Long press a link in your messages and read the real address.|Type your bank's address yourself and bookmark it.

v: Use mobile banking and wallets safely
Know what to do if money goes missing
Never share your PIN, card number with the back code, or codes
Use the official app from the official app store only
Set a daily transfer limit you are comfortable with
Turn on SMS or app alerts for every transaction

b.v: If your phone suddenly shows 'No service' for a long time when others around you have signal, someone may have taken a duplicate of your SIM. Call your telecom company and your bank at once.

Step by step:|Call your bank or wallet's official helpline immediately and ask them to block the account or card.|Note the time, amount and any messages.|Make a written complaint to the bank and keep the reference number.|Report it to the cyber crime authority.
Do this now:|Turn on transaction alerts.|Check your daily transfer limit in your banking app.

v: Lock down your phone
Control what apps can see
Screen lock with a PIN, pattern or fingerprint
Install system updates - they fix security holes
Install apps only from the official app store
Turn on the 'find my phone' feature

b.v: A torch app does not need your contacts. Check Settings > Apps > Permissions and remove access to camera, microphone, location, contacts and SMS from apps that do not need them.

v: Avoid banking on free public Wi-Fi
Use your own charger and cable in public places
Do not leave your phone unlocked with others

b.v: Do this now:|Check permissions of 5 apps and remove what they don't need.|Turn on 'find my phone'.

v: Share less about yourself
Know what to do if someone threatens you
Keep your profile private and accept only people you know
Don't post your CNIC, home address, travel plans or children's school
Never send private photos or videos to anyone - they can be saved and misused

b.v: 2) If someone blackmails or harasses you

Step by step:|Do not pay and do not send anything more - paying brings more demands.|Do not delete the chats: take screenshots with the date, name and profile link.|Block the person and report the account on the platform.|Tell a trusted family member.|Report it to the cyber crime authority (the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency, earlier the FIA Cyber Crime Wing). Check its official website for the current helpline and online complaint form.
It is not your fault. The law in Pakistan punishes online harassment and blackmail, and complaints can be made confidentially.
Do this now:|Set your social profiles to private.|Save the official cyber crime complaint website in your bookmarks.

day-9.t: Day 9 — Fake jobs and online shopping scams

v: Recognise job and earning scams
Shop online safely
A real employer does not ask you to pay for a job, visa or 'registration'
'Like videos and earn' or 'complete tasks' schemes that ask you to deposit money first
Investment groups promising fixed daily profit
Check overseas job offers only through licensed agents and official channels
Buy from known shops or sellers with real reviews
Prefer cash on delivery or safe payment through the platform when buying from a new seller
Never send advance money to a personal account for a 'too cheap' phone or bike
Check the parcel before paying the courier when allowed

b.v: Use the site's own chat and payment options, check the seller's ID-verified badge, and report anyone who asks you to pay outside the site.
Do this now:|Write 3 signs of a fake job offer.|Tell one young person in your family about task scams.

day-10.t: Day 10 — If something goes wrong: action plan

v: Know the exact steps after a hack or scam
Make a family safety plan

b.v: Step by step:|Use the 'forgot password' option to take it back.|Change the password and log out all other devices.|Turn on two-step login.|Tell your contacts not to trust messages from that account until it is fixed.|Report the hack to the platform.

Step by step:|Call your bank or wallet helpline at once - minutes matter.|Keep screenshots, numbers and transaction IDs.|File a written complaint with the bank and get a reference.|Report to the cyber crime authority with all the evidence.

v: A family rule: we never share codes, and we check money requests by phone
Parents and children can ask each other before tapping a strange link
Keep important helplines saved: your bank, your telecom company, cyber crime
Review phone settings of elderly parents once a month

b.v: Take the quiz to get your certificate, and share this course with your family - one shared lesson can save someone's savings.
Do this now:|Write your family safety plan in 5 lines.|Save the three helplines in your phone.
